plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A herbaceous perennial producing large, fragrant, bowl-shaped or double flowers on sturdy stems above deeply lobed, glossy green foliage. A beloved garden plant that can live for decades and returns reliably each year.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June)
plants.location: Native to Central and East Asia; widely cultivated in temperate gardens of North America and Europe
plants.funFact: Peonies have been cultivated in China for over 1,500 years, and a single plant can survive and bloom for more than 50 years.

plants.name: Rosa gallica
plants.description: A hardy, suckering deciduous shrub with fragrant, semi-double to double flowers and bright golden stamens. It is one of the oldest cultivated roses and a parent of many garden roses.
plants.location: Native to southern and central Europe and western Asia; grown in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Rosa gallica 'Officinalis', the Apothecary's Rose, was used medicinally in medieval times and its petals retain their fragrance when dried.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen subshrub with silvery-gray narrow leaves and dense spikes of small tubular flowers. It thrives in sunny, well-drained soils and is beloved by bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (June to August), beginning in southern regions in early June
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean region; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria and North America
plants.funFact: The name lavender comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning to wash, as the Romans used it to scent their baths.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub bearing the largest flower head in the Protea genus, with a central cone of tiny flowers surrounded by showy, petal-like bracts. It grows in fynbos vegetation on nutrient-poor soils.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere autumn to winter (March to August) with peak flowering in winter; blooming during June in South Africa
plants.location: Native to the Cape Floristic Region of South Africa
plants.funFact: The King Protea is South Africa's national flower, and its genus is named after the Greek god Proteus, who could change his shape.
